method: I rendered the whole part (overview.png, 1 m grid), the whole ground floor and the upper floor above for context, then 16 tiles of about 6.5 x 6 m at a 0.5 m grid with inserts and text. The tiles were x 7-13.5, 13-19.5, 19-25.5 and 25-32 in each of the rows y 20-26.2, 14.5-20.5, 9.5-15 and 5-10. I then made four close-ups: the west facade, the link's east end, the kitchen NW corner, and the corridor/lobby. I measured every candidate from prims.pkl with a small query script: wall line end points, JAMB and door-block inserts (_1D0L100, _1D3R90), and WIN/WALL-GL/D-JAMB frame pieces and panes. Two independent sweeps checked for misses. The first polygonized WALL+COL lines into wall cells and listed collinear gaps. The second searched every layer for quarter-circle arcs, which found the layer-0 swings of the north entrance, the pivot door and the shower door. A cluster pass over all WIN/WALL-GL/D-JAMB/DOOR items confirmed every glazing group is covered. Window vs door was decided from plan cues. For the main house's west face I also used the drawing's elev_left: it is a 2x-scale section through the glass link looking east (elev_x about 56.6 - 2*y). It shows the stair-hall glass, the link glass and the living-room west bays running from the floor. The upper plan was used only to compare the link glazing. a and b lie on wall centre lines at the structural wall/column faces. For glazing set in column lines I used the column axis, which the drawing's CENTER2 grid lines confirm, with thickness 0.25, and noted the 0.1 m frame line. The plan has no room names and no door or window tags (DSYM attributes are empty). The final renders check_all_final.png, check_west_final.png and check_east_final.png put a marker on every listed opening and glass wall; no unmarked gap, swing, leaf, jamb pair or window group is left in the box. I did not look at any other labeller's or detector's output.
